teething.title: Teething
teething.subtitle: Track teeth & comfort symptomsy
teething.symptomDroolingDesc: Excessive saliva production — very common during teething.
teething.symptomGumSwollenDesc: Red, inflamed gums at the eruption site.
teething.symptomIrritableDesc: Fussy, crying more than usual due to gum discomfort.
teething.symptomBitingDesc: Chewing on toys, fingers, or anything within reach.
teething.symptomSleepDisruptedDesc: Frequent night wakings due to pain.
teething.symptomRashDesc: Red rash on chin/neck from excess drool.
teething.symptomAppetiteDesc: Reluctance to eat due to sore gums.
teething.teethingRingNote: Silicone or rubber ring — chill in fridge (not freezer). The counter-pressure and cold soothe gums.
teething.coldWashclothNote: Wet a clean washcloth, twist and freeze 30 mins. The texture and cold provide relief.
teething.gumMassageNote: Use a clean finger to gently rub the gum for 1-2 minutes. Works quickly for immediate relief.
teething.chilledFeederNote: Fill a mesh feeder with frozen fruit or breast milk. Baby chews safely while getting cold relief.
teething.painReliefOTCNote: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Motrin) for babies 6+ months. Always consult your doctor first.
teething.amberBeadNote: Baltic amber contains succinic acid said to reduce inflammation. Use with supervision and never on a string around neck.
teething.otcDosageNote: Consult your pediatrician before giving any medication to babies under 6 months.
teething.tipFrozenRingBody: Freeze a silicone teething ring for 30 mins. The cold numbs gums safely. Never freeze gel-filled rings.
teething.tipBitingBody: Baby's gums are inflamed — biting applies counter-pressure. Offer cold washcloths, silicone toys, or wooden teethers.
teething.tipDroolRashBody: Excess drool causes chin/neck rash. Pat dry frequently, apply petroleum jelly as barrier, keep a soft bib on.
teething.tipFeverBody: Teething may cause slight fever (<38°C / 100.4°F). Higher fevers are NOT normal — consult your doctor.
teething.tipNightWakingBody: Teething pain peaks at night. Try cold gum massage before bed, and keep the room cool (68-72°F / 20-22°C).
teething.tipFirstToothBody: Start brushing when first tooth erupts. Use a tiny smear of fluoride toothpaste on a soft infant toothbrush.

milkPrep.title: Milk Prep
milkPrep.noBagsAvailable: Add bags to your stash first.
milkPrep.tipRefreezeBody: No. Once thawed, milk must be used within 24h (fridge) or 2h (room temp). Never refreeze.
milkPrep.tipTransportBody: Use an insulated cooler with frozen ice packs. Milk stays safe up to 24h. Keep cooler closed as much as possible.
milkPrep.tipAddFreshTitle: Can I add fresh to leftover?
milkPrep.tipAddFreshBody: Cool fresh milk first, then combine. Use within 2h of when the oldest milk was first exposed to room temp.

reflexTracker.title: Reflex Tracker
reflexTracker.subtitle: Track primitive reflex integration
reflexTracker.alertBody: {{reflexes}} {{has}} persisted beyond expected window. Consult your pediatrician.
reflexTracker.emptyBody: Record your baby's primitive reflexes and monitor when they naturally integrate as the nervous system matures.
reflexTracker.aboutText: Primitive reflexes are automatic movements present at birth that typically disappear (integrate) as the baby matures. Tracking them helps identify developmental progress and flag when reflexes persist beyond typical windows.
reflexTracker.moroDesc: Startle response — arms extend outward when startled
reflexTracker.palmarDesc: Involuntary grip when palm is touched
reflexTracker.plantarDesc: Toe curling when sole is stroked
reflexTracker.babinskiDesc: Upward toe fan when sole is stroked (after 2 years = normal)
reflexTracker.galantDesc: Trunk incurvation when back is stroked
reflexTracker.steppingDesc: Walking motion when held upright with feet touching surface
